label: SiSAAS
summary: Multi-tenant SaaS — NestJS + Postgres RLS, Next.js, worker, Kafka events
nextSteps: git init && git add -A && git commit -m 'initial commit'

mono.label: Single deployable
mono.description: One app: identity, features and web together. Events are delivered in-process — no Kafka to operate. Start here.

identity.label: Microservice — identity
identity.description: Owns users, tenants and memberships. The ONLY service that issues tokens.

service.label: Microservice — feature service
service.description: Verifies tokens, holds no user records, keeps a local tenant projection fed by events.

options.label: Multi-tenant
options.description: Many organisations in one database, isolated by Postgres RLS.

options.label: Single organisation — a normal web app
options.description: No tenant column, no RLS, no memberships. Users, and your own tables.
notes: No RLS means no `pnpm verify:rls` — the isolation it proves does not exist here, and a gate that passes vacuously is worse than none.
Going multi-tenant later is a migration, not a flag: every table needs a tenant column, a backfill and a policy.

options.label: Built-in (NestJS)
options.description: Users, tenants, memberships and JWT in this codebase. No extra service to run.

options.label: Keycloak
options.description: Full OIDC provider — realms, federation, MFA, social login. A service to operate.
notes: Create a realm and a confidential client, then set OIDC_ISSUER and OIDC_AUDIENCE.
Map your tenant claim to `tenantId` in the client's token mapper — the guard reads it from there.

options.label: ZITADEL
options.description: OIDC provider whose organisation model maps onto tenants directly.
notes: Organisations map to tenants. Add a custom claim carrying the org id as `tenantId`.

options.label: None — I will write it
options.description: No auth module and no guards. Endpoints are unprotected until you add something.
notes: Every route is open. The tenant id has no trusted source, so RLS has nothing to scope by until you provide one.

options.label: MinIO
options.description: S3-compatible, self-hosted. In the dev stack already.

options.label: External S3
options.description: AWS S3 or any compatible provider. Nothing to run locally.
notes: Set S3_ENDPOINT, S3_ACCESS_KEY and S3_SECRET_KEY to your provider's values.

options.label: None
options.description: No file storage. The media module is removed.

options.label: Presigned S3 URLs
options.description: The browser uploads straight to storage. Simplest, and bytes never touch the API.

options.label: tusd (resumable)
options.description: Resumable uploads over the tus protocol. For large files and unreliable connections.
notes: tusd stores to the same S3 bucket and calls back on completion — the hook is authenticated with a shared secret.
Worth it when uploads are large or the network is poor; a presigned PUT is simpler for anything small.

options.label: None — BullMQ is enough
options.description: The template already has BullMQ for background jobs measured in seconds.

options.label: Temporal
options.description: Processes measured in days: onboarding, payouts, retries with human steps.
notes: Workflow code must be deterministic — no Date.now(), no Math.random(), no direct I/O. Side effects go in activities.
Put the tenant id in the workflow id rather than using a namespace per tenant.

options.label: None
options.description: Structured logs and metrics only. Add one later with `si add`.

options.label: Umami
options.description: Page analytics, no cookies, GDPR-friendly. The lightest option.

options.label: PostHog
options.description: Analytics, feature flags and session replay in one service.
notes: Identify users by an opaque id, never by email — an analytics store is a lower-trust environment than your database.

options.label: OpenReplay
options.description: Session replay — see exactly what the user did before the bug.
notes: Replay records what users type. Mask every personal-data field and never record an auth screen BEFORE enabling this in production.

options.label: k6
options.description: Load tests as code, with thresholds that fail CI.

options.label: None
options.description: Add it later with `si add k6` when there is load worth testing.

options.label: None
options.description: No payments. Add one later with `si add`.

options.label: KPay
options.description: Mobile Money, card and PayPal across 12 African countries. USSD prompt or hosted link.

options.label: JoonaPay
options.description: PaymentIntents with signed webhooks.

options.label: KPay and JoonaPay
options.description: Both configured; requests route by currency and method.
notes: `selectProvider` routes by currency and method, and refuses rather than guessing when neither can settle a request.
